title: design: the board's emotional layer, with a voyage chart, a service record, rituals and the kraken
acceptance: The captain settled the emotional layer in a design session on 2026-09-24. The first feeling is companionship, then accomplishment. Every emotional beat maps to a real event: no invented progress, no random or timed celebration. Information density and the 13px/16px type floors are unchanged. This task extends prototype v2 (T-070) with that layer, as design only, for the captain to approve before implementation tasks are opened. Its own entry must be committed into design/tasks.json and its row added to design/design.md's task table on this task's branch.

Voyage chart, always visible as a slim band under the ship. Milestones are ports with nautical names (set in config), and hovering shows the real milestone. The ship's position comes from merged tasks. Ready tasks are islands on the route ahead; clicking one opens its card, and 'set course' equals answering the readiness card with proceed, so several choices form a route in order. Backlog tasks are islands behind reefs labelled with the task they wait on. Open GitHub issues are uncharted islands in fog: 'survey' has firstmate draft a spec and raise a spec card, approval clears the fog, and 'skip' leaves the island in the fog.

Crew service records and ranks, from real events only. The crew is one fleet across projects, with a project badge showing where a crewman is now. Workers rise from deckhand through able seaman (3 merged), bosun's mate (10), bosun (25) to quartermaster (50), with first-pass reviews weighted. Reviewers rise from apprentice inspector through inspector to chief inspector by approvals never later overturned. Thresholds live in config, and outfit and pennant change with rank.

Rituals, each under two seconds, each switchable off, each triggered by a real event. Arriving at a port with fireworks when a milestone completes. A salute when a task passes on the first review. The captain's greeting on the day's first visit, one sentence of true numbers ('早安，船長。昨夜入港三艘，兩張卡等你定奪，海面平靜。'). Clearing skies and a cheer when a red check turns green. Failures appear as weather the crew works through together, never as a crewman's fault.

The kraken. One at a time, it appears when a task reaches review round three without approval. It has one tentacle per stuck task, at most 8, each labelled with its task id and opening that card on click. With nothing stuck it shows only as a shadow far off. The tone is menacing but a little comic. Outcomes follow the captain: dropping or rescoping a task makes the kraken flee (dropping sends it down whole; rescoping shrinks it and leaves it in the distance while work remains). Choosing to resolve it starts an intense battle that follows real progress: a rejected round is the kraken striking the deck, a new push is a hit, a red check thickens the storm. When the worker and reviewer finally get the approval, the battle is won, with an animation and a synthesised victory fanfare of about 4 seconds, played once per approval. A battle of three or more rounds earns a line in the next day's greeting. Honours from real resolutions are written into the service record.

Combat mode on the live board: clicking a tentacle opens the stuck task's real actions (re-dispatch, park, rescope, proceed). Only a confirmed action lands a blow, the animation always follows the real action and never creates one, and the whole sequence stays under three seconds.

Playground mode: a switch on the board shows a clear Playground banner. Everything can be triggered freely there: times of day, weather, rates, handoffs, rituals, ranks, port arrivals, and a fake kraken to fight with an aim-and-time cannon game. Nothing is written and no real state is touched; turning it off returns to the live state at once.
Sound: every sound, including a new optional ambient layer of sea, rigging and gulls that follows weather and time, is off until the captain turns it on.

Issues and tags, settled with the captain on 2026-09-24. Every open issue of the target repository is synced. The issues get a lane of their own, 'Issues', to the left of backlog: an issue is not a task until firstmate has drafted a spec and the captain has approved it, so raw issues never mix with specced work. The same issues are the fog islands on the voyage chart. Surveying an issue has firstmate draft a spec and raise a spec card. On approval the task enters backlog or ready carrying its '#n issue' tag, and, when the project's registry entry sets issues.auto_close (default true), its pull request body says 'Closes #n', so merging closes the issue; with auto_close false the body says 'Refs #n' and the issue stays open. 'Skip' hides an issue from the lane without touching GitHub. Tags combine on one card in a fixed order: project, then origin (chat, issue or skill update, each its own colour), then '#n issue', then '#n PR'. Issue and PR numbers link to their pages on that project's repository. A task born in chat can become an issue: at the captain's request, firstmate drafts the title and body from the spec and raises a card. Only on approval is the issue created in the target repository and its '#n issue' tag added. Nothing is ever created on GitHub without that card.

Battle mini-game, settled on 2026-09-24. During a real battle (a task at review round three or later without approval) the captain can play along with skills. Skills affect only the battle, never real work: only an approval from the worker and reviewer wins, and real work changes only through the task card's real actions. Six skills, all available from the start: broadside (click a tentacle with timing; better timing does more damage; cooldown 8s); chain-shot (drag a line across two tentacles to bind both and pause their attacks; 15s); harpoon (hold to charge, release for a heavy blow on one tentacle; 12s); full-sail evade (space bar; the ship turns away from a slam; 10s); captain's order (click the captain; the crew's attacks double for 5 seconds; 30s); repair (click a damaged deck section; 6s). Every skill works with keyboard and touch. The skill bar and effects follow the frontend-design skill and v2's visual language. The playground carries the same game against a fake kraken.

Decision-card diagram that follows the chosen option, restored from prototype v1 (captain, 2026-09-24). The v1 card had a 'Diagram' panel showing BEFORE → AFTER for the option the captain picks, with 'pick an option first' before any choice. Neither the live board nor v2 does this. v2's decision cards gain that panel in its visual language: it switches instantly as options A–D and custom are picked, and the authored overall diagram stays above it as the overview.

Battle intensity and the controls panel (captain, 2026-09-24). The battle must feel fierce, and the current skill effects are too plain: every skill gets a distinct, heavy effect, with explosions as the centrepiece (flash, shockwave ring, debris and embers, smoke, screen shake, hit-stop), layered per skill and scaled to the skill's weight, within the reduced-motion rule. Hits land on the kraken's head, which is the only hit target: the tentacles carry card information (task ids that open cards) and must never be hit, covered or obscured by any effect. The prototype's option controls (state switches, playground, sound) move into a floating panel that can be hidden and shown with one control, so the ship and the battle stay in view without scrolling up and down. Every kraken attack in the mini-game is telegraphed before it lands (a readable wind-up: the head rears, the target spot glows, a short warning cue), long enough to react. The captain can dodge it, and a successful dodge opens a short window for a powerful counterattack with its own bigger explosion. Each kraken attack shows a wind-up progress bar, so the moment to dodge is readable rather than guessed; the bar has a narrow 'perfect' zone near its end. The fight rewards reading, not mashing: the kraken has several attack patterns, each with its own telegraph and bar speed (a slow slam, a quick jab, a two-hit combo, and a feint whose bar stops short and punishes an early dodge), and it mixes them more as the real review rounds climb. A normal dodge opens a short counter window; a perfect dodge (inside the zone) adds a brief slow-motion beat, exposes a weak point on the head, and makes the counter a critical hit with the largest explosion. Chained perfect dodges build a counter combo. Every one of these stays inside the battle and never touches real work.

Decision cards as strategy-game cards (captain, 2026-09-24). The captain's decision cards stop being plain boxes and look and move like cards in a strategy card game, while keeping every piece of information they carry now, including the before→after diagram of the chosen option. A card arrives dealt onto the table (slide and flip), has a framed face whose border and emblem follow its kind (merge, scope, choice, readiness) and its urgency, and tilts toward the pointer with a foil glare on hover. Each option is its own playable card in a hand: hovering lifts it, picking it plays it onto the table, where the diagram panel flips to that option's before→after, and confirming seals the decision with an impact effect before the card is taken off the table. The information panel (title, explanation, pros and cons, outcome, the diagram, PR and tags) stays a legible, flat, fully readable face at the 13px/16px floors; effects frame it and never cover text. Every effect is under one second, follows a real action, respects reduced motion, and its sound stays off until the captain turns sound on. Motion specs are delivered for each.

Deliver these in the same proposal folder: the prototype updated with switches that demonstrate every state above, plus the motion and sound specs for each new element. Evidence is the required GitHub check and the seven gates. Stay inside this scope.
